skill.name: ensembl-database
skill.description: Query the Ensembl genome database REST API for gene lookup, sequence retrieval, variant annotation, comparative genomics, and assembly mapping.
skill.summary: Access Ensembl genomic data for genes, variants, sequences, orthologs, species, and assemblies.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Genomic researchers need reliable access to Ensembl data without memorizing every endpoint. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through gene, variant, sequence, and comparative genomics queries.
actual_capabilities: Look up Ensembl gene records by symbol or Ensembl identifier.
Retrieve genomic, transcript, coding, or protein sequences in supported formats.
Query known variants and run VEP-style consequence lookups through Ensembl endpoints.
Find orthologs, paralogs, and gene tree information for comparative genomics work.
Inspect genomic regions for features such as genes, transcripts, or variants.
Map coordinates between genome assemblies such as GRCh37 and GRCh38.
limitations: Requires network access to public Ensembl REST API services.
Results depend on Ensembl release data and endpoint availability.
Large batch jobs must respect Ensembl rate limits and retry guidance.
Does not replace clinical interpretation or variant curation by qualified experts.

use_cases.title: Annotate genes for research
use_cases.description: Look up gene coordinates, transcripts, proteins, and cross references for a target gene list.

use_cases.title: Evaluate variant consequences
use_cases.description: Query known variants and retrieve predicted molecular effects for research reports.

use_cases.title: Compare genes across species
use_cases.description: Find orthologs and related sequences to support comparative genomics analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Look up a gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Ensembl database skill to look up BRCA2 in human. Summarize the gene location, stable ID, transcripts, and key cross references.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve sequence data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ensembl to retrieve the genomic sequence for ENSG00000139618. Explain which endpoint you would use and note the expected output format.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ensembl resources to inspect rs699 in human. Report population data when available and summarize predicted molecular consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Build a comparative workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Ensembl workflow to compare human BRCA2 with mouse orthologs, retrieve sequences, and map relevant coordinates between assemblies.

output_examples.output: A concise gene report with the Ensembl stable ID, chromosome location, available transcripts, and links to related database references.

output_examples.input: Find orthologs for a human Ensembl gene ID in mouse.
output_examples.output: A comparative summary listing matching mouse genes, homology type, species names, and suggested next steps for sequence comparison.

output_examples.input: Map a GRCh37 coordinate to GRCh38.
output_examples.output: An assembly mapping explanation that states the source assembly, target assembly, mapped coordinate, and any unmapped result notes.

best_practices: Use stable Ensembl identifiers when possible because gene symbols can be ambiguous.
Respect Ensembl rate limits and use batch endpoints for repeated lookups.
Record species, assembly, and Ensembl release information with every result.
anti_patterns: Do not treat API results as clinical guidance without expert review.
Do not run large unthrottled query loops against public Ensembl services.
Do not mix GRCh37 and current assembly coordinates without explicit mapping.

faq.question: What database does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the public Ensembl REST API and related Ensembl documentation for genomic data access.

faq.question: Can it query non-human species?
faq.answer: Yes. Ensembl supports many species, and the skill includes species-aware examples and workflows.

faq.question: Does it support variant analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide variant lookup and Variant Effect Predictor style consequence queries through Ensembl endpoints.

faq.question: Can it retrieve FASTA sequences?
faq.answer: Yes. The included examples show sequence retrieval in JSON and FASTA-style formats where supported.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: No API key is described for the standard public Ensembl REST API examples in this skill.

faq.question: Is it safe for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. It supports research workflows, but clinical interpretation requires validated pipelines and qualified review.
